noticias.titular: An MIT committee calls for rethinking aims, assessment and the in-person community in the face of an AI that can already do almost any written work
noticias.entradilla: The ad hoc committee of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology proposes eight principles and a set of recommendations for adapting university teaching to generative AI.
noticias.imagen_alt: A diagram with a top bar of eight principles from which three arrows lead to three columns: educational processes (oral exam, portfolio), community (a group of people) and support structures (organisation chart and tools).

noticias.titular: A report for UNESCO proposes replacing “at what age?” with “for what purpose and on what evidence?” when using AI in the classroom
noticias.entradilla: Sonia Livingstone and three co-authors argue that there is no single right age for using AI in education and call for decisions based on child development and clear educational aims.
noticias.imagen_alt: A box with the question “At what age?” crossed out in red and an arrow towards three items in a column (“Purpose?”, “Conditions”, “Evidence”); below, “About / with AI”, a balance with a book in one pan and a screen in the other.

noticias.titular: The World Economic Forum sets out seven practices to make AI safe for children without shutting them out of learning
noticias.entradilla: A September 2026 document from the Global Coalition for Digital Safety takes children’s well-being, and not merely the absence of incidents, as its goal, and proposes practices for those who design AI and incentives to ensure they are followed.
noticias.imagen_alt: A schematic temple: the pediment reads “Child well-being”; below it, “Seven practices”, seven columns, and resting on a slab, “Seven incentives”, seven blocks with icons (report, contract, coin, flask, public building, padlock and cycle) holding it up.

noticias.titular: Catalonia sets out 45 guidelines on which uses of AI to promote and which to limit in schools
noticias.entradilla: The Department of Education and Vocational Training publishes a guide in September 2026 that advises against autonomous use of general-purpose AI by under-14s, grading with AI and AI-text detectors.
noticias.imagen_alt: Diagram in two columns: on the left, “Under 14”, a teacher operates the screen while students look on; on the right, “14 to 18”, a student uses the screen with a family authorisation form. Below, uses in assessment: “Permitted”, creating instruments and marking closed answers, and “Prohibited”, grading and using detectors.

noticias.titular: Catalonia offers criteria for deciding when a technology adds value in primary and ESO, and places AI in the fourth year
noticias.entradilla: The Department of Education’s guide puts technology at the service of learning, with decision tables, progression by cycle, digital well-being and criteria for selecting resources.
noticias.imagen_alt: A funnel with “Seven criteria” for decision-making sends an arrow towards a staircase of five steps, “Growing autonomy” for students; only the top step is highlighted: “AI in year 4” of ESO.
